messages:
Alex (Partnerships): Quick sync — we need a concise telemetry/contract for connectors that captures backpressure, queueing, and throttling signals. Goal: single schema we can share with Snowflake/Databricks/vector DB partners for marketplace readiness.
Sara (Partner Eng): +1. Partners keep asking how we surface 'connector health' in marketplace UI. Backpressure visibility is the missing piece.
Mike (Infra): Do we mean queue length, consumer lag, and retry rate? Also want a sample cardinality for tags so we don't blow up metrics costs.
Jin (Runtime): For our serving runtime we can emit: prefix_cache_hit, request_enqueue_time_ms, dequeue_latency_ms, max_inflight_per_model. But SDKs need a stable semantic mapping.
Alex (Partnerships): Exactly. Proposed minimal fields: connector_id, partner, region, metric, value, unit, sample_rate, tags[]. Optional: event_type (gauge | counter | histogram) and backpressure_reason.
Anna (Solutions): Customers want actionable alerts (e.g., "connector stalled due to ingestion throttling"). Can we include an optional sample payload of last-error-code and a short error_message? Helps SIs triage.
Mike (Infra): Agree on error_code. On cardinality: tags should be limited to 3-4 high-cardinality dims (model_version, deployment_zone, partner_tier). Others as low-card.
Sara (Partner Eng): For partner docs we'll need a compatibility matrix: Snowflake connector supports request_enqueue_time_ms and backpressure_reason; Databricks supports enqueue + dequeue; Qdrant/Milvus support consumer_lag and retry_rate. We should list what each partner can emit initially.
Alex (Partnerships): Good call. I'll draft the compatibility table. Who can own the schema PR and a lightweight JSON Schema?
Jin (Runtime): I'll take the JSON Schema and a sample SDK mapping for the runtime (<1 week). Will include guidance on sampling and batching.
Mike (Infra): I'll add Prometheus/OTLP exporter examples and a small query snippet for latency percentile SLA checks.
Anna (Solutions): I'll draft the marketplace UI text explaining what backpressure means and suggested remediation steps for customers + SI playbook notes.
Sara (Partner Eng): We should loop in partner PMs before we finalize. Suggest a 30-min partner sync next Wed. I'll send invites.
Alex (Partnerships): Thanks. Quick sketch of JSON Schema I'm dropping here for feedback:
```json
{
  "connector_id": "string",
  "partner": "string",
  "region": "string",
  "metric": "string",
  "value": "number",
  "unit": "string",
  "sample_rate": "number",
  "tags": ["string"],
  "event_type": "string",
  "backpressure_reason": "string",
  "error_code": "string",
  "error_message": "string",
  "timestamp": "ISO8601"
}
```
Mike (Infra): Looks good. Add a required field list (connector_id, metric, value, timestamp). Also recommend max tag cardinality enforcement in SDK.
Jin (Runtime): Noted. For runtime telemetry we'll map `request_enqueue_time_ms` -> metric: "enqueue_latency_ms" and `dequeue_latency_ms` -> "dequeue_latency_ms". We'll publish mapping table.
Sara (Partner Eng): I'll prep the partner-facing doc and include example dashboards for Snowflake and Databricks.
Alex (Partnerships): Action items: Jin JSON Schema + SDK mapping (due 1945683000), Mike exporter examples + query snippets (due 1945683000), Sara invites & partner doc (due 1945682000), Anna marketplace blurb + playbook snippet (due 1945682000).
deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: telemetry-schema-draft -> staging at 1945681200.
Alex (Partnerships): Great — if we can get the draft into staging before partner sync we can iterate with them. Tagging @partners to review once Sara has invites. :eyes: :shipit:
Sara (Partner Eng): Will do.
